input:
An amine absorption unit was evaluated at pilot scale using gas from a cement kiln. During a test lasting 45 days, the unit operated at 13 t of carbon dioxide per day and captured 85% of the carbon dioxide contained in the treated gas. The associated steam demand was 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, while solvent loss amounted to 1.7 kg per tonne captured. These results provide a picture of the unit's capture performance and utility and solvent requirements under the conditions of the pilot test. However, the period beyond 45 days was not covered by the reported testing. In particular, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent over a longer period remains untested, so the solvent behaviour observed during the test should not automatically be extended to longer operation without further evidence.

The figures are most useful when kept on the basis on which they were measured. Capture performance is expressed relative to the carbon dioxide in the treated gas, while the utility and solvent figures are normalised to the amount captured, so they describe different aspects of the same test rather than interchangeable measures of throughput. The pilot scale and kiln source also matter to the interpretation: the test shows how the unit behaved on that gas stream and over that operating period, but it does not by itself establish long-duration solvent stability. Dust is identified as the specific unresolved issue because it could affect solvent condition beyond the period for which measurements were reported. Until that effect is tested, the proper conclusion is limited to the performance and consumption values actually observed during the pilot run.
target:
An amine absorption unit tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln captured 85% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. The test ran for 45 days at 13 t of carbon dioxide per day. Steam demand was 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured; solvent loss was 1.7 kg per tonne captured.

The capture figure is the share removed from the treated gas under the pilot conditions, and the steam and solvent figures are stated per tonne captured rather than per tonne treated. The three results therefore describe one operating basis: capture performance, energy input, and solvent consumption over the same test. The result is limited to the tested period. Beyond 45 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent is untested, so neither continued solvent condition nor performance over a longer run is established by this test.

The basis matters. Capture is stated relative to carbon dioxide in the treated gas; steam demand and solvent loss are stated per tonne captured. The results can therefore be used together for the pilot condition, but they do not convert the test into a long-run solvent assessment. Kiln dust is the named unresolved exposure. Its effect on the solvent beyond the test period is unknown from this work, and the reported solvent loss should not be read as evidence that later losses will follow the same rate. The test establishes performance and consumption over its own duration on cement-kiln gas at pilot scale. Longer solvent behaviour remains a separate question requiring a longer test. That separation keeps the measured operating result distinct from an unmeasured ageing effect in the solvent.
